evidence_items.explanation: Meta's 2025 capex was very large. But it is company-wide capex, not the cost of one model 'experiment', and it says nothing about whether the money was wasted.

receipt.public_excerpt: “xAI was not built right first time around, so is being rebuilt from the foundations up,” Musk said Thursday on his social media platform, X.

evidence_items.explanation: Confirms the Musk statement the post relies on. It is an organizational admission, not a cost figure or a finding that the spending was lost.

receipt.public_excerpt: In internal tests, Avocado fell short of leading models from Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic in logical reasoning, programming, and writing.

evidence_items.explanation: Supports the post's premise that Meta's model was 'good but not great' at the time of the post. It does not measure cost or waste.

receipt.public_excerpt: The benchmark results published alongside the launch paint a picture of a model that is competitive but not dominant.

evidence_items.explanation: Within a month of the post, Meta's spending produced a model reported as competitive. That weighs against a plain 'money down the drain' reading, but whether the cost was worth it remains a judgment.

unresolved_gaps: No source gives a defined cost for Meta's or xAI's model 'experiment' as distinct from company-wide AI infrastructure spending.
No reliable public figure for xAI's total AI spending was read and cited.
No objective test exists for whether the spending went 'down the drain'. The infrastructure stays in use, and returns will keep coming in over years.
